To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single type of proprioceptive mechanoreceptor can be used to encode the position and motion of a tactile sensor, and that this information can be transmitted to higher brain centers by a population of descending inter-neurons that can be modeled using only a few computational elements.
a single type of antennal hair encodes both antennal motion and position, and that a large variety of interneurons in the descending mechanosensory pathway are able to integrate this information.

a) we have quantified responses of all important descending mechanosensory interneurons to changes in antennae position, motion and movement direction, b) we have identified the two most important features of this response variability, and c) we have developed a computational model that can account for the response properties of the entire descending interneuron population, using the hair-field model as its only source of input.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a mechanistic understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying tactile sensing and active tactile exploration.
the neural basis of active tactile sensing in insects, and the role that mechanoreceptive information about position and motion of tactile sensors plays in the generation of adaptive motor responses.
the analysis of a neural pathway that transmits proprioceptive information from mechanosensory hair fields to motor networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is able to explain the coding-space and response properties of a complete descending neural network.
the proposed computational model of the descending pathway can be considered as a proof of principle for a mechanistic explanation of how tactile sensing is mediated in insects.
the proposed model of the descending mechanosensory pathway provides an accurate description of the response properties of a population of interneurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a computational model of a descending mechanosensory pathway, which explains how proprioceptive mechanosensors are used to encode the position and motion of the antennae.
the coding-space of a complex neural network is spanned by two PCs, and that the response properties of this network can be explained by a single input model.
we have developed a framework that can model a complete descending mechanosensory pathway in the stick insect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coding-space of the entire pathway can be captured by a simple two-dimensional model.
a simple mechanosensory input can be processed in the CNS in a complex way, and that this complexity can be captured by a computational framework.
the diversity in the response properties of the entire DIN pathway can be explained by a simple, biologically plausible computational model.
